source_text: In diem sabbati sancti Ἀμφιλοχίου ἐπισκόπου Ἰκονίου λόγος τῷ ἁγίῳ σαββάτῳ. Ἐπιτάφιον ἑορτὴν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἑορτάζομεν σήμερον. Καὶ ὁ μὲν παρὰ τοῖς νεκροῖς κάτω τοῦ θανάτου τὰ δεσμὰ διαλύων καὶ φωτὸς τὸν ᾅδην πληρῶν καὶ ἀφυπνίζων τοὺς κεκοιμημένους, ἡμεῖς δὲ χορεύομεν ὑπὲρ γῆν τὴν ἀνάστασιν φανταζόμενοι καὶ οὐ δεδοίκαμεν τὴν φθοράν, μὴ κατισχύσῃ τῆς ἀφθαρσίας. Οὐ δώσεις γάρ, φησίν, τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν. Καὶ ἴσως ἡμῶν τὴν φιλοσοφίαν γελῶσι Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ Ἕλληνες· οἱ μὲν ἕτερον Χριστὸν προσδεχόμενοι, οἱ δὲ τάφοις ἐναποκλείσαντες αὐτῶν τὰς ἐλπίδας, περὶ ὧν εἰκότως ὁ προφήτης φησίν· Οἱ τάφοι αὐτῶν οἰκίαι αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ἀλλ' οἱ μὲν γελῶντες στενάζουσι–στενάξουσι γὰρ ὕστερον ὁρῶντες εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν καὶ ἐξύβρισαν–, ἡμεῖς δὲ δακρύοντες ἡδονῇ τὸ πάθος κεράσωμεν. Ἥρπασεν ὁ θάνατος τὸν δεσπότην Χριστόν, ἀλλ' οὐ καθέξει παρ' ἑαυτῷ τὴν ζωήν. Κατέπιεν ἀγνοήσας, ἀλλ' ἐξεμέσει πολλοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ. Ἑκὼν κατέχεται νῦν, μετὰ ταύτην τὴν ἡμέραν σκυλεύσας τὸν ᾅδην ἀνίσταται. Χθὲς ἠμαύρωσε τὸν ἥλιον σταυρωθεὶς καὶ μεσούσης ἡμέρας ἐπεισῆλθεν νύξ, σήμερον ὁ θάνατος παραλύεται ξένον νεκρὸν εἰσδεξάμενος. Χθὲς ἐπένθησεν ἡ κτίσις τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων μανίαν ὁρῶσα καὶ στολὴν πενθικὴν τὸ σκότος ἐνεδύσατο, σήμερον ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκότει φῶς εἶδε μέγα.
thought_title: The feast of the tomb and the hidden despoiling of Hades
orientation: The preacher opens the homily for Holy Saturday, addressing the congregation as they celebrate the burial feast while Christ is below among the dead.
pass_a_gloss: For the day of the holy Sabbath, a discourse of Amphilochius bishop of Iconium, for the holy Sabbath. We celebrate today a funeral feast of our Saviour. And he on the one hand, below among the dead, loosening the bonds of death and filling Hades with light and waking those who have fallen asleep, we on the other hand dance above the earth, imagining the resurrection, and we do not fear decay, lest it prevail over incorruption. For you will not give, he says, your holy one to see decay. And perhaps Jews and Greeks laugh at our philosophy: the ones awaiting another Christ, the others having shut up their hopes in tombs, about whom fittingly the prophet says: Their tombs are their houses forever. But the ones laughing will groan—for they will groan later, seeing him whom they pierced and insulted—, but we, weeping, let us mix the passion with pleasure. Death seized the master Christ, but it will not keep life with itself. It swallowed without knowing, but it will vomit out many with him. Willingly he is held now; after this day, having stripped Hades, he rises. Yesterday he darkened the sun, having been crucified, and at midday night came in; today death is undone, having received a strange corpse. Yesterday creation mourned, seeing the madness of the Jews, and put on darkness as a mourning garment; today the people sitting in darkness saw a great light.

choices.why: The adjective means 'over the tomb' or 'funeral'; with 'feast' it names the paradoxical celebration of Christ's burial.
The perfect participle of 'sleep' is the standard Christian euphemism for the dead; keeping the metaphor preserves the waking image.
The verb means to picture or form an image in the mind; 'imagining' keeps the sense of present mental anticipation of the resurrection.
ξένος means foreign, strange, or unfamiliar; 'strange' captures the paradox that this corpse is unlike any other, which is the point.
The passive of παραλύω means to be loosened, weakened, or undone; 'is undone' fits the personified death being disabled.

choices.english: let us mix the passion with pleasure
choices.why: The hortatory subjunctive with 'passion' (Christ's suffering) and 'pleasure' (the joy of the feast) preserves the paradox of mourning and rejoicing.
rejected: let us blend the suffering with delight
let us temper the passion with pleasure

pass_b_english: Today we celebrate a funeral feast for our Saviour. He is below among the dead, loosening the bonds of death, filling Hades with light, and waking those who have fallen asleep, while we dance above the earth, imagining the resurrection. We do not fear that decay will prevail over incorruption, for the prophet says, “You will not let your holy one see decay” (Psalm 16:10). Perhaps the Jews and the Greeks laugh at our wisdom: the Jews because they wait for another Christ, the Greeks because they have shut up their hopes in tombs. Of them the prophet rightly says, “Their tombs are their houses forever” (Psalm 49:11). But those who laugh will groan—later they will groan when they see the one they pierced and insulted. As for us, let us mix the passion with pleasure as we weep.

Death seized the master Christ, but it will not keep life with itself. It swallowed without knowing, but it will vomit out many along with him. Christ is held willingly now; after this day he will strip Hades and rise. Yesterday, when he was crucified, he darkened the sun, and night came in the middle of the day. Today death is undone, having received a strange corpse. Yesterday creation mourned when it saw the madness of the Jews and put on darkness as a garment of grief. Today the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light (Isaiah 9:2).

problems.why: The Greek says Christ lies now; English adds ‘held willingly’ which is not in the source.
problems.ruling: Ἑκὼν κατέχεται means 'willingly he is held/detained,' but 'held willingly' distorts: ἑκών modifies the subject (he lies willingly), not passive 'is held willingly' by another.

fixed: The Greek 'Ἑκὼν κατέχεται νῦν' means 'willingly he is held now'; the English 'Christ is held willingly now' already conveys this. The suggested 'Christ lies now' omits 'willingly' and is less accurate. No edit needed.

problems.why: 'κατέχεται' is passive 'is held/detained', not 'lies'. Christ is being held willingly, not merely lying.
problems.ruling: Greek κατέχεται = ‘is held/detained’, not ‘lies’; changes meaning of Christ’s state.

problems.quote: Death seized the master Christ, but he will not keep life with him.
problems.source_quote: Ἡρπασεν ὁ θάνατος τὸν δέσποτην Χριστόν, ἀλλ' οὐ καθέξει παρ' ἑαυτῷ τὴν ζωήν.
problems.why: Subject of 'will not keep life' is death, not Christ; English misattributes agency.
problems.fix: Death seized the master Christ, but it will not keep life for itself.
problems.ruling: ἀλλ' οὐ καθέξει: subject is death (ὁ θάνατος), but English 'he will not keep' implies Christ.

edits.old: but he will not keep life with him
edits.new: but it will not keep life with itself

fixed: Changed 'Christ lies willingly now' to 'Christ is held willingly now' because the source 'κατέχεται' is passive, meaning 'is held/detained', not 'lies'.
Changed 'but he will not keep life with him' to 'but it will not keep life with itself' because the subject of 'οὐ καθέξει' is death (ὁ θάνατος), not Christ; the English misattributed agency.

problems.why: English 'He swallowed without knowing' makes 'He' the subject of swallowing, but ἀγνοήσας is masculine singular, agreeing with θάνατος (death) from prior clause. Death swallowed without knowing. English 'He' ambiguously refers to Christ due to prior clause about Christ being held. This is misleading.
problems.ruling: Greek subject is death (θάνατος); English ‘He’ misleads to Christ, changing meaning.

fixed: Changed 'He swallowed without knowing' to 'It swallowed without knowing' because the Greek participle ἀγνοήσας is masculine singular, agreeing with θάνατος (death) from the preceding clause, not with Christ. The English 'He' was ambiguous and misleading.

problems.why: Intro says Psalm 15 is Psalm 16 in modern Bibles, but text quotes Psalm 16:10; reader may think these are different psalms.
problems.fix: Clarify Psalm 15 LXX = Psalm 16 MT in all citations.

problems.why: Multiple terms for same group; 'those who dared it' and 'they' in early section may not connect to 'the Jews' later.
problems.fix: Keep 'the Jews' consistent or gloss 'those who dared it'.

problems.quote: the Greeks because they have shut up their hopes in tombs
problems.why: Intro calls them mockers; in the sermon they 'shut up hopes in tombs'—same group, different framing.
problems.fix: No change needed; variants are consistent in reference.

problems.fix: Check Greek; likely 'joy' or 'gladness' better fits the context.
